newsitem.title: USA: Mass Gov proposes $18.2 bln budget for FY 1998.
newsitem.headline: Mass Gov proposes $18.2 bln budget for FY 1998.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld on Wednesday proposed an $18.2 billion budget for fiscal year 1998 that raises spending by 2.9 percent and includes seven new tax cuts that are worth $82 million for that year.
The governor, in prepared remarks, said the new budget marks another step in a turnaround engineered by his Administration.

"Six years ago, when we took office, our bond rating had plummeted, our Rainy Day fund was bankrupt, and we were almost $2 billion in the red. Today, we are $700 million in the black, our Rainy Day fund is full and this balanced budget, our eighth consecutive, gives more money than ever back to the taxpayers and cities and towns in the Commonwealth," he said.

Weld, who lost a close and costly race to U.S. Sen. John Kerry, might set aside his longstanding belief in term limits and run for a third term as governor, but has only raised $34,289 for his gubernatorial account, ending the year with a $70,000 balance, Boston Globe said Wednesday. The governor's fund is much smaller than the $1.3 million amount raised by Lieutenant Gov Paul Cellucci.

The new fiscal budget includes $50 million in sewer rate relief and another $55 million in Lottery distributions, providing $3.8 billion in local aid to cities and towns. And the budget includes a plan to abolish county governments, an effort the Weld Administration has renewed due to a recent default on $4.7 million of notes by Middlesex County.
The tax cuts that Weld proposed are:
--Phasing out over five years the five percent sales tax on telecommunications, worth $16 million.
--Eliminating the net investment income tax on domestic insurance companies, worth $15 million.
--Reducing over five years the 12 percent tax on "unearned income to 5.95 percent, worth $27 million.
--Setting the investment tax credit rate permanently at three percent.
--Increasing the dependent tax deduction for children to $1,600 from $600, worth $12 million.
--Setting up a $3,500 job training tax credit for employers, worth $5 million.
--Exempting military retirement pay from the state income tax, valued at $7 million.
